payload.text:
THE THREE DEPENDENCY BUDGETS ARE HELD BY A TEST RATHER THAN BY DISCIPLINE. `opt/prez/crate/tests/manifest.rs` asserts the dependency table of every manifest in the workspace against the budget hv approved for it, and fails the build when one moves: the root `Cargo.toml` (prez -- `comrak` and `artifact`, AC02); `crates/showreel/Cargo.toml` (the nine of AC-3.9); `crates/artifact/Cargo.toml` (EMPTY, which that manifest's own comment calls "a contract rather than a current fact").
ONE RULE, THREE INSTANCES, AND COVERING ONE WOULD HAVE BEEN AN INSTRUMENT REPORTING SOMETHING ADJACENT TO WHAT WAS NEEDED. AC-3.9 names showreel's manifest alone because that is the manifest it is about. The hole it describes -- a written budget with no enforcement, true today and false the moment a line is added, with nothing going red -- is identical in all three, and a gate covering a third of the population while reading as "the manifest budget is enforced" is the failure this thread has now recorded seven times across three nodes.
AND AC-3.9 POINTS AT THE WRONG HOME, WHICH IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO MISLEAD. Its text says "the natural home for an actual gate is issue 0016, already scheduled by hv as a WP-05 rider". Issue 0016 is about `manifest.sha256` -- the INSTALL manifest -- recording which CI gates were green at publish time. Read end to end it names no crate, no dependency and no `Cargo.toml`. Two unrelated things share the word "manifest", vc wrote the collision into a satisfied row, and a reader sent to 0016 for the dependency gate would find a publish-provenance rider and conclude it was covered.
NAMES ARE NOT THE BUDGET, SO A NAME-SET CHECK WOULD NOT HAVE HELD IT. `image`'s defaults pull every decoder in the crate (+35 against the five features actually listed) and `qrcode`'s pull an image backend the tool has no use for (+8 against +1 for svg alone) -- so DROPPING `default-features = false` blows the budget while leaving the name set identical. The gate therefore asserts the full whitespace-normalised line for every entry, not the key. Brittleness to cosmetic edits is the intended behaviour and not a defect: any change to an approved line returns to hv, which is what AC-3.9's rule already says in words. Nothing reformats these files -- the pre-commit formatter takes staged markdown only.
THE GATE REFUSES WHAT IT CANNOT READ, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A DETECTOR RATHER THAN A CENSUS. A hand-rolled parse that fails to recognise a line omits it silently, and the test then passes having measured a smaller population than it named -- the fourth kind of zero, and the one this contract has caught most often. So: every non-blank non-comment line inside a dependency table must parse as `name = value` or the test FAILS naming the line and the file; a dependency table whose header is missing FAILS rather than reading as an empty set, without which `artifact`'s expected-empty assertion is a tautology that a broken parse would satisfy; and `[dev-dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]` must be ABSENT from all three, because the budget is denominated in lockfile packages and those spend it too.
`fast_image_resize` IS ASSERTED REFUSED IN BOTH PLACES IT COULD APPEAR: absent as a dependency name in all three manifests, and absent as a package entry in the tracked `Cargo.lock`. AC-3.9's evidence has made that measurement by hand twice, both times correctly; making it once, mechanically, is what the row is for.
THE GATE ITSELF TAKES NO DEPENDENCY, AND THAT IS A CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A FLOURISH. A TOML crate would have to enter as a dev-dependency of `prez`, whose budget is `comrak` and nothing else -- so the instrument enforcing AC02 would have had to breach AC02 to exist. std only, hand-rolled against a closed grammar, in the house style the root manifest already documents for args and front matter.
RED-PROOF REQUIRED BEFORE THIS ROW SATISFIES, NOT AFTER. All three manifests are correct today, so a gate written today goes green on its first run and that green proves nothing. Every assertion is proved by breaking the manifest it reads, observing the named failure, and reverting.
BUILT AND RED-PROVED BY vc 2026-09-10 09:04Z. `opt/prez/crate/tests/manifest.rs`, 210 lines, std only, five tests green. It sits in the workspace ROOT package because the property is workspace-wide and because `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` reaches all three manifests plus `Cargo.lock` from there without climbing out of a crate.
EIGHT MUTATIONS, EIGHT REDS, EACH NAMING ITS OWN FAILURE -- RUN AGAINST THE REAL MANIFESTS, NOT AGAINST FIXTURES. (1) `itoa = "1"` added to showreel's nine; (2) `default-features = false` dropped from `image`; (3) a dependency added to `artifact`'s empty table; (4) `artifact`'s `[dependencies]` header deleted -> "has no [dependencies] table -- the gate refuses to read that as an empty budget"; (5) a `[dev-dependencies]` table added to the root; (6) showreel's `regex` renamed to `fast_image_resize`; (7) `qrcode` rewritten as a multi-line inline table -> "the manifest gate cannot read this line inside [dependencies], so it cannot say whether the budget holds: }"; (8) a second crate added to prez, which is AC02's budget rather than AC-3.9's. Every manifest restored with `git checkout --` and the tree verified clean after each.
THE MUTATIONS RAN THE ALREADY-BUILT TEST BINARY DIRECTLY RATHER THAN THROUGH cargo, AND THAT IS METHOD, NOT A SHORTCUT. `cargo test` re-resolves the workspace when a manifest moves, which would have rewritten `Cargo.lock` eight times and rebuilt `image` with every decoder for probe (2). The gate reads its files at RUNTIME, so the binary answers the same question with nothing else moving.
PROBE (2) IS THE ONE THAT JUSTIFIES ASSERTING WHOLE LINES, AND ITS SUPPORTING CLAIM WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: with `default-features = false` dropped from `image`, the dependency NAME SET IS BYTE-IDENTICAL -- nine names before, nine after, `diff` empty. **A name-set gate stays green while the budget goes from five decoders to every decoder in the crate.** That is the adjacency this row was written to avoid, and it is now demonstrated rather than argued.
TWO TESTS PROVE THE PARSE ITSELF, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE OTHER THREE DETECTOR GREENS RATHER THAN CENSUS GREENS. `a_missing_table_is_not_an_empty_one` fixes `None` against `Some(vec![])` on synthetic text; `a_line_the_gate_cannot_read_is_refused_rather_than_skipped` fixes the multi-line refusal. Without the first, `artifact`'s expected-empty assertion is satisfied by any parse broken enough to find nothing.
THE ONE HALF NOT PROVED BY MUTATION, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the `Cargo.lock` half of the `fast_image_resize` assertion. Probe (6) fired on the MANIFEST half, because the lock genuinely carries zero occurrences and inserting a fake package stanza would have been rewritten by the next resolve. So that assertion is a literal `contains` against a file measured at 0 -- true, and untested in the failing direction. It is a second lock on a door probe (6) already holds shut, and it is recorded here as unproven rather than counted as one of the eight.
AND THE GATE'S REAL LIMIT, WHICH IS NOT A DEFECT BUT MUST NOT BE MISREAD: a change to a manifest AND to this list in the same commit passes. The gate cannot make a change approved; it makes an unapproved one IMPOSSIBLE TO MAKE QUIETLY -- the budget now lives in a file a reviewer must touch, in a diff, next to hv's name. That is the whole distance between discipline and a gate, and it is the distance AC-3.9 asked for.
SUITE AFTER: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` 283 passed, 0 failed, across five binaries; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0. The gate adds a sixth test target and no dependency to any of the three budgets it enforces.
